example_prompt: Transcribe a short Wolof or Swahili voice note (under 60 seconds) and get the transcript in the same response.

audio_file_blob.description: The audio file. The field table types it as String, 'url to a readable file', but every documented example uploads a local file as a multipart file part (curl --form 'audio_file_blob=@"/C:/Users/aaaa/file.wav"'). Supported formats: .wav, .mp3, .mp4, .m4a, .ogg, .webm, .flac.

use_language_asr_input.description: set the input language code. Codes from the Supported Languages page (61 languages). African languages: af (Afrikaans-English), ak (Akan-English), am (Amharic-English), ar (Arabic), bem (Bemba), ff (Fulani), fuc (Fulani (Pulaar)), fuf (Fulani (Pular)), fub (Fulani (Adamawa Fulfulde)), fuv (Fulani (Nigerian Fulfulde)), fuq (Fulani (Central-Eastern Niger Fulfulde)), fue (Fulani (Borgu Fulfulde)), ffm (Fulani (Maasina Fulfulde)), gaa (Ga), ha (Hausa-English), ig (Igbo-English), lg (Luganda-English), nso (Northern Sotho), nyn (Nyankole), om (Oromo), pcm (Pidgin-English), rw (Kinyarwanda-English-French), sn (Shona), st (Sotho), sw (Swahili-English), tn (Tswana), tw (Twi), wo (Wolof-English), xh (Xhosa), yo (Yoruba-English), zu (Zulu-English), luo (Dholuo (Luo)), kr (Kanuri), ki (Kikuyu), nup (Nupe), ti (Tigrinya). Code-switched models (Code-switched table): af, ak, am, ha, ig, lg, pcm, rw, sw, wo, yo, zu.

gotchas: The API key comes from the developers tab of your account on voice.intron.io; send it as 'Authorization: Bearer {key}' from your backend only — the docs say never expose it in client-side code.

Duration limit is contradictory: the page says 'only supports files durations less than or equal to 120 seconds', but its documented 400 says 'audio duration of 65seconds exceeds the max duration of 60seconds'. Keep audio under 60 s here, or use submit_audio_transcription for anything longer.

A 503 is not necessarily a failure: the request can time out after 120 seconds with HTTP 503 and data.file_id (body status "Error", message "file queued for processing"). The docs say this file_id can be used to get the file's status — call get_transcription_status with it.
The body is multipart/form-data, not JSON. Every option is a form field whose value is the string "TRUE" or "FALSE" — not a JSON boolean.

use_category defaults to file_category_telehealth, not file_category_general — set it explicitly. The docs list the get_* options of each category (see each option's description); what happens with an option from another category is not documented.

audio_file_blob is typed 'String — url to a readable file' in the field table, but every example uploads the file itself (curl --form 'audio_file_blob=@"path"'). Send the file; passing a URL is not shown anywhere.

use_language_asr_input is 'required: yes' in the upload tables, but the Question Answering page lists it as optional with default 'en', and both the custom-template example and the English Python sample on upload/sync omit it. Always send it — per the Question Answering page, a missing code means 'en'.

get_answer=TRUE treats the audio as a spoken question and returns only transcript_answer: all other post-processing options are ignored. The answer is in the question's language unless use_language_data_extraction_output sets another code. When no question is detected, transcript_answer is not an answer: the model 'briefly acknowledges what was said and invites the user to ask a question' (documented example: "Good morning! I'm here to help..."). The Question Answering page marks get_answer as required, the upload tables as optional (default FALSE).
get_icd_codes output has two names in the docs: transcript_icd_codes in the procedure examples, transcript_billing_codes in the completed example on Get File Status. Read both.

No dedicated response field is documented for get_differential_diagnosis, get_followup_instructions or get_practice_guidelines: in the completed example on Get File Status their output appears as sections inside transcript_suggestions.

The body's status is "Ok" on success and "Error" on failure (the balance endpoint returns "success"). message is not a reliable signal: some 200 examples carry "file queued for processing" next to a finished transcript.

Only two error bodies are documented (400 duration limit and 503 timeout, both on upload/sync). The status code and body for an invalid API key, an unknown file_id, a rate-limit hit or exhausted credits are not documented, nor is a maximum file size.

The public docs describe no sandbox, test key, free tier or pricing, and don't say how file transcription is billed: every call hits production. The account's credit balance is readable with get_credits_balance.
Rate limit: 30 requests per minute on upload/sync. Responses carry rate-limit headers; Retry-After gives the delay in seconds before retrying.

spans: This endpoint only supports files durations less than or equal to 120 seconds
The request can timeout with an http status code 503 and the file-id in 120 seconds
